subject: Graceful decommitment & ramp escrow: executive variance request
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@medtrix.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@medtrix.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:15 -0700
Subject: Proposed ramp + graceful decommitment language (Medtrix)

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Procurement wants to make progress on the SOW, but we need a single executive-level ask cleared: a narrow graceful decommitment clause and a ramp/downsizing protection in case Medtrix materially changes product direction in the first 9 months. The legal team attached a short redline of a proposed ramp schedule and a simple opt-out with an escrowed credit bucket.

High level of Medtrix proposal:
- 90-day partial unwind window (staged reductions every 30 days) with capped penalty credits up to 20% of committed spend.
- Opt-out triggers: material regulatory change or product sunset; 60-day notice.
- Ramp support: a 3-month onboarding credit and access to a sandbox for up to 2 engineers.

They're asking for an executive variance on standard Redwood ramp/termination terms and a modest one-time onboarding credit. Can you escalate to deal desk + sales leadership? Attached: Medtrix_Mutual_Action_Plan_v3.pdf (redlines) and ramp_schedule_redline.docx.

I can jump on a 15-min call if helpful.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Director, Procurement — Medtrix

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:03:42 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposed ramp + graceful decommitment language (Medtrix) — need exec variance

Folks — forwarding Medtrix's ask. TL;DR: procurement wants a limited decommitment/downsizing path within the first 9 months plus a small onboarding credit (3 months) and sandbox access. They propose a staged 30-day reduction cadence with capped credits equal to 20% of committed spend.

Why I'm escalating:
- This is non-standard for our committed reserve terms (we typically allow a narrow off-ramp only at specific milestones).
- The requested cap would reduce revenue by an estimated $85k NRR in year 1 if exercised.
- They are a strategic healthcare prospect (integration with core EMR) — losing the account now could cost more pipeline/diffusion.

Ask: 
1) Executive variance for a constrained graceful decommitment window (approve/deny).
2) If approve, confirm the maximum credit cap we can accept and the exact notice period.
3) Approval to offer the onboarding credit ($X figure below) OR propose an alternative (e.g., credits applied to Professional Services rather than MRR).

Recommendation (my read): Approve a conditional variance with these guardrails: 60-day notice, staged reductions at 30/60/90 days up to 15% capped credit, onboarding credit limited to $25k applied to PS, and full audit clause (usage logs retained 12 months). This keeps us protected while providing flexibility.

Attached redlines from Medtrix. I can circulate a clean amendment for signature if we land on the parameters.

Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
(prior: enterprise sales ops)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed ramp + graceful decommitment language (Medtrix) — need exec variance

Priya — thanks for the summary and redlines. Read the doc and ran a quick revenue sensitivity. My take: we should avoid a 20% cap — that's too open. We can accept the concept of a staged ramp but with stricter constraints to limit revenue leakage and moral hazard. Proposed counter (high level):

- Accept staged reductions at 30/60/90 days but cap total refunds/credits at 12% of committed value for the first 9 months (reconciled against usage).
- Notice: 60 days but only effective for the next billing cycle (i.e., no immediate pro-rata refunds beyond reconciled credits).
- Onboarding credit: offer up to $20k in one-off PS credit or 40 developer hours applied as PS, not MRR. Sandbox access as part of our standard POC offering (no extra charge).
- Require signed MPA amendment and a 6-month data retention/audit provision (logs for 12 months) so we can validate usage.

Legal redline notes: two items for Karthik/legal to confirm — (1) whether we can accept their proposed trigger language (product sunset/regulatory) without opening an operational exception, and (2) the audit clause language.

If Sean signs off on the cap and PS-credit approach, I can turn this into a clean one-page amendment for quick signature.

Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Deal Desk — Redwood Inference

Marking this approved with conditions. I spoke briefly to Finance and Legal. Final approval parameters below — these are the executive-level variance and should be captured in the amendment language exactly as written.

Executive variance — approved conditions:
1) Cap the total credits/allowances to 12% of committed ARR for the first 9 months (reconciled against actual usage).
2) 60-day written notice required; reductions take effect at the start of the next billing cycle.
3) Onboarding credit: one-time PS credit not to exceed $20,000; sandbox access included for up to two engineers for 90 days.
4) Implement a usage audit right: Medtrix consents to log retention for 12 months and a quarterly reconciliation during the first 9 months. Failure to cooperate voids the variance.
5) Any material regulatory-trigger language will be limited to explicitly defined, agreed-upon regulations (Legal to supply list); generic "regulatory change" triggers are unacceptable.
6) Deal to include a clause that the variance is a one-time concession and cannot be used as precedent for other customers.

Karthik/Legal — please draft the amendment with these points and the redlines for signature. Marissa/Priya — once Legal sends the amendment, loop in Alicia for a final quick call to confirm.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
(sean cell: +1 650-555-0287)
